# Spec: Mutations + auto-generated Input types — the `DjangoMutation` write-side foundation, the shared `FieldError` envelope, and `create` / `update` / `delete` on the DRF-shaped `class Meta` surface

Shipped in `0.0.11` (card [`DONE-036-0.0.11`][kanban]). This card opens the package's **write side** — the single largest unscoped gap against [`strawberry-graphql-django`][upstream-mutations], which ships `create` / `update` / `delete` + auto-generated `Input` / `PartialInput` types and the package has none of. It lands the mutation *foundation*: a [`DjangoMutation`][glossary-djangomutation] base class configured through a nested `class Meta` (the DRF shape, not Strawberry decorators), [auto-generated `Input` / `PartialInput` types][glossary-input-type-generation] derived from `Meta.model` that honor the relation-override contract pinned in [`DONE-010-0.0.4`][kanban] ([`spec-010`][spec-010]), and the shared [`errors: list[FieldError]`][glossary-fielderror-envelope] envelope — defined here as the **one** `FieldError` type every flavor returns, so the form-based (`0.0.12`) and DRF-serializer / auth (`0.0.13`) flavor cards attach it unchanged. The write resolvers run sync and async, scope `update` / `delete` lookups through the target type's [`get_queryset`][glossary-get_queryset-visibility-hook] + [`apply_cascade_permissions`][glossary-apply_cascade_permissions] ([`DONE-034-0.0.10`][kanban]), re-fetch the mutated row through [`DjangoOptimizerExtension`][glossary-djangooptimizerextension] for the response selection, and resolve the return / input target through the model's **primary** [`DjangoType`][glossary-djangotype] ([`Meta.primary`][glossary-metaprimary], [`DONE-018-0.0.6`][kanban]). **Version boundary** (see [Decision 13](#decision-13--version-bumps-are-owned-by-the-joint-0011-cut)): this card shares the `0.0.11` patch line with [`DONE-037-0.0.11`][kanban] (the [`Upload` scalar][glossary-upload-scalar] + file / image field mapping, which maps the same model fields to `Upload` on the mutation input side this card generates); the `pyproject.toml` / `__version__` / [`tests/base/test_init.py::test_version`][test-base-init] bump to `0.0.11` is owned by the **joint cut**, not by this card. No slice in this card bumps the version.

Status: **SHIPPED (`0.0.11`)** — card [`DONE-036-0.0.11`][kanban], released under the [`CHANGELOG.md`][changelog] `## [0.0.11]` heading; all five slices final-accepted. Authored from the card body via the [`docs/SPECS/NEXT.md`][next] flow. The [Slice checklist](#slice-checklist) below stays unticked because the `Status:` line is the completion source of truth (the shipped-spec convention). ## Key glossary references

Skim these [`docs/GLOSSARY.md`][glossary] entries first — they anchor the vocabulary used throughout the spec:

- [`DjangoMutation`][glossary-djangomutation] — the subject. The glossary already pins its planned contract: a base class with `Meta`-driven configuration, auto-generated `Input` / `PartialInput`, the shared `FieldError` envelope, sync + async resolver paths, and optimizer composition for the post-write return value. This card ships exactly that contract; the entry is promoted from `planned for 0.0.11` to `shipped (0.0.11)` in Slice 5.
- [Input type generation][glossary-input-type-generation] — the surface Slice 1 builds. The entry pins two generated types: `Input` (the `Model.objects.create(...)` shape — a field is required only when it has no usable Django `default` / `blank` / `null`, else optional; **not** a blanket "every field required") and `PartialInput` (every field optional, matching `Model.objects.update(...)` semantics), both preserving the relation-override contract from the foundation slice. [Decision 6](#decision-6--auto-generated-input--partialinput-types) realizes it.
- [`FieldError` envelope][glossary-fielderror-envelope] — the shared error contract. `errors: list[FieldError]` returned by every mutation flavor, each `FieldError` carrying a `field` path, `messages: list[str]`, and the two additive default-empty client-ergonomics lists `codes: list[str]` / `path: list[str]`, populated from `form.errors` / `serializer.errors` / a `ValidationError` raised inside the write path. This card **defines** it ([Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper)) as the single shared type [`DjangoFormMutation`][glossary-djangoformmutation] (`0.0.12`) and [`SerializerMutation`][glossary-serializermutation] (`0.0.13`) return unchanged; it may only ever grow **additive, default-empty** fields, so a client selecting `field` / `messages` is never broken by a later flavor.
- [`DjangoType`][glossary-djangotype] / [`Meta.primary`][glossary-metaprimary] / [`Meta.model`][glossary-metamodel] / [`Meta.fields`][glossary-metafields] / [`Meta.exclude`][glossary-metaexclude] — the type system the mutation target rides. The **return type** resolves the model's **primary** `DjangoType` through the registry primary lookup ([Decision 11](#decision-11--primary-type-resolution-return-type-and-input-target-resolve-the-models-primary-djangotype)); the **input-field set**, by contrast, derives from the model's *editable* fields narrowed by the mutation's own `Meta.fields` / `Meta.exclude` — **not** the read `DjangoType` selection ([Decision 6](#decision-6--auto-generated-input--partialinput-types), Medium-4).
- [`get_queryset` visibility hook][glossary-get_queryset-visibility-hook] / [`apply_cascade_permissions`][glossary-apply_cascade_permissions] — the permission seams `update` / `delete` lookups compose with. A `DjangoMutation` cannot mutate a row the target type's `get_queryset` (plus any cascade) hides; the lookup runs through the same visibility queryset every read surface uses, so a hidden row is "not found", never an existence leak ([Decision 10](#decision-10--permission-composition-update--delete-lookups-run-through-the-target-get_queryset)).
- [`DjangoOptimizerExtension`][glossary-djangooptimizerextension] / [`only()` projection][glossary-only-projection] / [FK-id elision][glossary-fk-id-elision] / [Queryset diffing][glossary-queryset-diffing] — the post-write re-fetch cooperation. The mutated row is re-fetched as a queryset the optimizer plans for the response selection. Because the operation is a **mutation**, the [`spec-035`][spec-035] **G2** gate keeps `select_related` / `prefetch_related` but suppresses `.only(...)` column deferral — so the re-fetched instance carries no selection-shaped deferred-field set and post-write consumer code touching an unprojected field never triggers a deferred refetch or a deferred-instance partial `save()` ([Decision 9](#decision-9--optimizer-composition-and-the-spec-035-g2-live-test-handoff)).
- [`DjangoConnectionField`][glossary-djangoconnectionfield] / [`DjangoListField`][glossary-djangolistfield] / [`DjangoNodeField`][glossary-djangonodefield] — the existing field-factory family `DjangoMutationField` joins. Each is a factory assigned to a class attribute on an `@strawberry.type`; the write-side factory follows the same idiom rather than inventing a decorator ([Decision 5](#decision-5--public-surface-djangomutation-base--djangomutationfield-factory--fielderror-exported-from-the-root)).
- [`FilterSet`][glossary-filterset] / [`OrderSet`][glossary-orderset] / [`RelatedFilter`][glossary-relatedfilter] — the prior set-family subsystems whose layout, finalizer phase-2.5 binding, stable class-derived input naming, and materialize-before-`Schema` lifecycle this card mirrors ([Decision 4](#decision-4--module-and-test-locations-mutations-subpackage-mirroring-filters--orders) / [Decision 12](#decision-12--finalization-seam-register-at-class-creation-bind-at-phase-25-no-deferred_meta_keys-change)).
- [`finalize_django_types`][glossary-finalize_django_types] / [Definition-order independence][glossary-definition-order-independence] — the once-only finalization gate the mutation binding hangs off; generated input / payload classes must be materialized before the schema is constructed, exactly as the filter / order input classes are.
- [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] / [`SyncMisuseError`][glossary-syncmisuseerror] — the two validation / misuse exceptions this card raises: `ConfigurationError` at mutation-class creation (bad `Meta`, unknown operation, model with no registered primary type), and `SyncMisuseError` when a sync write path meets an `async def` target `get_queryset` (the same discipline the Relay node defaults and the cascade helper already follow).
- [Scalar field conversion][glossary-scalar-field-conversion] / [Choice enum generation][glossary-choice-enum-generation] / [Specialized scalar conversions][glossary-specialized-scalar-conversions] / [`auto`-typed annotations][glossary-auto-typed-annotations] — the converters the input generator reuses; a model field becomes an input field of the same scalar / enum the read-side `DjangoType` would synthesize, so the wire contract is symmetric across read and write.
- [`Upload` scalar][glossary-upload-scalar] / [`DjangoFileType`][glossary-djangofiletype] / [`DjangoImageType`][glossary-djangoimagetype] — the sibling `0.0.11` card ([`DONE-037-0.0.11`][kanban]); it maps `FileField` / `ImageField` to `Upload` on the **input** side this card generates, so the two cards share the `0.0.11` cut and a thin input-converter seam ([Decision 13](#decision-13--version-bumps-are-owned-by-the-joint-0011-cut), [Out of scope](#out-of-scope-explicitly-tracked-elsewhere)).
- [`DjangoFormMutation`][glossary-djangoformmutation] / [`DjangoModelFormMutation`][glossary-djangomodelformmutation] / [`SerializerMutation`][glossary-serializermutation] / [Auth mutations][glossary-auth-mutations] — the downstream flavor cards (`0.0.12` / `0.0.13`) that consume this card's `DjangoMutation` base and `FieldError` envelope unchanged; named here only to fix the reuse contract this card freezes.
- [Per-field permission hooks][glossary-per-field-permission-hooks] / [`FieldSet`][glossary-fieldset] / [Cross-subsystem invariants][glossary-cross-subsystem-invariants] — the `1.0.0` invariant this card must not violate: deferred `Meta` keys are promoted only when their subsystem applies them end-to-end. This card adds no `DjangoType` `Meta` key, so [`DEFERRED_META_KEYS`][types-base] is untouched ([Decision 12](#decision-12--finalization-seam-register-at-class-creation-bind-at-phase-25-no-deferred_meta_keys-change)).

Project conventions to follow:

- [`AGENTS.md`][agents] — the test-placement rule (package-internal mutation mechanics under [`tests/mutations/`][test-mutations] mirroring source; live consumer behavior earned over `/graphql/` in [`examples/fakeshop/test_query/`][test-query-dir]); the live-HTTP-priority coverage rule (the write side **is** live-reachable the moment products exposes a `Mutation`, so Slice 4 is mandatory, not optional — it is also the [`spec-035`][spec-035] G2 handoff); the no-pytest-after-edits rule; the CHANGELOG-edit-permission rule at [`AGENTS.md`][agents] #"No CHANGELOG.md updates unless told" — Slice 5's release-note edit must be named in its maintainer prompt.
- [`START.md`][start] — "Meta classes everywhere on consumer surfaces. If you find yourself writing stacked Strawberry decorators on a consumer-facing class, stop. That is the strawberry-graphql-django API and the explicit reason this package exists." This is the decisive rule for [Decision 3](#decision-3--class-meta-surface-not-decorators-borrow-the-capabilities-reject-the-decorator-surface). Also: the "behaviorally we copy strawberry-graphql-django's good ideas, surface-wise we copy django-graphene-filters" rule, and the reference-style markdown link convention (defs at the bottom under the 10 canonical group headers).
- [`CONTRIBUTING.md`][contributing] — the 100% coverage target (`fail_under = 100`); every branch of the input generator, the resolver pipeline, and the error path earns coverage in [`tests/mutations/`][test-mutations] plus the live products suite.
- [`docs/TREE.md`][tree] — the target layout already reserves `django_strawberry_framework/mutations/` (planned by this card) and `tests/mutations/`; this card creates those trees and adds no module outside them beyond the products-example wiring.
- [`GOAL.md`][goal] — the `1.0.0` showcase and the DRF-migration shape both spell the mutation surface as `class CreateCategory(DjangoMutation): class Meta: ...` (the serializer flavor lands `0.0.13`); this card ships the model-driven base that shape rests on.

## Slice checklist

Each top-level item maps to one commit / PR. **Five slices: input generation + envelope (Slice 1), the `DjangoMutation` base (Slice 2), the resolvers + field factory (Slice 3), the products live write surface (Slice 4), and the doc + card wrap (Slice 5).** Slices 1–3 are package-internal and mutually staged (each builds on the prior); Slice 4 is the live consumer surface and the [`spec-035`][spec-035] G2 handoff; Slice 5 is doc-only.

- [ ] Slice 1: input-type generation + the `FieldError` envelope + the payload wrapper (per [Decision 6](#decision-6--auto-generated-input--partialinput-types) / [Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper))
  - [ ] [`mutations/inputs.py`][mutations-inputs]: a BFS-free, single-model input factory that, given a model's **editable** fields (narrowed by the mutation's own `Meta.fields` / `Meta.exclude`, **not** the read `DjangoType` selection — Medium-4), generates `<Model>Input` (each field required **only when it has no usable default** — no `default`, `null=False`, `blank=False` — else optional with `strawberry.UNSET`; Major-1) and `<Model>PartialInput` (every field optional, defaulting to `strawberry.UNSET`). Editable-field selection excludes the pk, `auto_now` / `auto_now_add` / `editable=False` columns, and reverse relations; forward FK / OneToOne become a single `<field>_id` input typed as the target's id (`GlobalID` for a Relay-Node target, else the raw pk scalar); M2M becomes `list[<id>]`. The canonical full editable shape takes the stable `<Model>Input` / `<Model>PartialInput` name; a narrowed (`Meta.fields` / `Meta.exclude`) shape takes a deterministic shape-derived name, and two distinct shapes colliding on one name raise [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] (AR-H1 / AR-M6) — all materialized as module globals so identical shapes dedupe.
  - [ ] The public `FieldError` `@strawberry.type` (`field: str`, `messages: list[str]`, plus the additive default-empty `codes: list[str]` and `path: list[str]`) and the generated `<Name>Payload` wrapper (the mutated object in the uniform `node` / `result` slot — `node` for a Relay-Node target, `result` otherwise, AR-H5 — nullable, plus `errors: list[FieldError]!`).
  - [ ] The relation-override contract from [`spec-010`][spec-010] holds on the input side: a consumer-authored input field is honored, not clobbered by a generated one.
  - [ ] Package coverage: [`tests/mutations/test_inputs.py`][test-mutations] — required/optional field shapes, FK/O2O/M2M id mapping, pk/auto-field exclusion, Relay-vs-non-Relay id type, stable naming for the full shape + shape-derived naming and collision `ConfigurationError` for narrowed shapes (AR-H1 / AR-M6), the `node` / `result` payload slot (AR-H5). The consumer-`input_class`-follows-the-generated-scheme pins (AR-M2) live in [`tests/mutations/test_sets.py`][test-mutations] with the rest of the `Meta` validation matrix, where Slice 2's coverage bullet claims them.
- [ ] Slice 2: the `DjangoMutation` base + `Meta` validation + finalizer binding (per [Decision 5](#decision-5--public-surface-djangomutation-base--djangomutationfield-factory--fielderror-exported-from-the-root) / [Decision 12](#decision-12--finalization-seam-register-at-class-creation-bind-at-phase-25-no-deferred_meta_keys-change))
  - [ ] [`mutations/sets.py`][mutations-sets]: `DjangoMutation` + its metaclass — collect `Meta` (`model`, `operation`, optional `input_class` / `partial_input_class` / `fields` / `exclude` / `permission_classes` / `select_for_update` — the row-lock opt-out, default `True`, a non-bool rejected at class creation), validate at class-creation (unknown `Meta` key; **no resolvable model** — in `0.0.11` a missing `Meta.model`, via the overridable `_resolve_model` seam so the `038` / `039` flavors can supply it differently, [Decision 5](#decision-5--public-surface-djangomutation-base--djangomutationfield-factory--fielderror-exported-from-the-root); `operation` not in the three model-flavor values [`mutations/operations.py`][mutations-operations] derives (`create` / `update` / `delete`); an `input_class` that is not a `@strawberry.input`-decorated type, or whose field names diverge from the generated scheme — AR-M2 → [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror]); `permission_classes` defaults to `[DjangoModelPermission]` (the write-auth seam, AR-H3 / [Decision 15](#decision-15--write-authorization-a-drf-shaped-check_permission--metapermission_classes-seam)), register the mutation, and bind it at [`finalize_django_types`][glossary-finalize_django_types] phase 2.5 (resolve the model's primary type, materialize the generated input / payload classes before the schema is constructed, raising [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] on a duplicate generated name — AR-M6).
  - [ ] No change to [`DEFERRED_META_KEYS`][types-base] / `ALLOWED_META_KEYS`: a mutation `Meta` is its own validation namespace, not a `DjangoType` `Meta` key ([Decision 12](#decision-12--finalization-seam-register-at-class-creation-bind-at-phase-25-no-deferred_meta_keys-change)).
  - [ ] Package coverage: [`tests/mutations/test_sets.py`][test-mutations] — `Meta` validation matrix, registration, finalizer binding, the no-registered-primary-type error.
- [ ] Slice 3: the write resolvers + `DjangoMutationField` + optimizer / permission composition (per [Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async) / [Decision 9](#decision-9--optimizer-composition-and-the-spec-035-g2-live-test-handoff) / [Decision 10](#decision-10--permission-composition-update--delete-lookups-run-through-the-target-get_queryset))
  - [ ] [`mutations/resolvers.py`][mutations-resolvers]: the sync + async create / update / delete pipeline — decode the `data:` input (and `id:` for update / delete) with relation `GlobalID` **type-checked against the target model** (wrong-type → `FieldError`, AR-H4), **authorize** via `check_permission` / `Meta.permission_classes` (before validation for create, after the visibility lookup for update / delete, denial → top-level `GraphQLError`, AR-H3 / [Decision 15](#decision-15--write-authorization-a-drf-shaped-check_permission--metapermission_classes-seam)), run `full_clean()` (on update, `exclude=<unprovided>` **minus fields co-constrained with a provided field** — AR-H2), write + assign M2M (replace-on-provide / clear-on-empty / unchanged-on-omit, AR-M1), re-fetch / snapshot through the optimizer, return the payload — with **locate→snapshot inside one `transaction.atomic()`**, itself nested in the completion-spanning transaction the schema's execution context opens for the mutation field, every error-envelope return marking that transaction for rollback before it builds the payload, and the async path in a single `sync_to_async(thread_sensitive=True)` call (AR-M4); a Django `ValidationError` — incl. the `validate_constraints()` `UniqueConstraint` violation caught before `save()` (Major-2), multi-field constraints keyed to the `"__all__"` sentinel (AR-M3) — populates the `FieldError` envelope and returns a null object, and a concurrent-race `IntegrityError` maps to the same envelope as a documented fallback.
  - [ ] [`mutations/fields.py`][mutations-fields]: `DjangoMutationField(MutationClass)` — the field factory (the write-side sibling of [`DjangoConnectionField`][glossary-djangoconnectionfield]) that synthesizes the resolver signature (`data: <Model>Input!` / `<Model>PartialInput!` + `id:` per operation) and returns a `strawberry.field(...)`; the one synthesized resolver dispatches sync or async **at runtime** via `in_async_context()`, the runtime half of the async detection [`DjangoListField`][glossary-djangolistfield] uses, so one factory output serves `schema.execute_sync` and `await schema.execute` alike.
  - [ ] `update` / `delete` lookups run through `target_type.get_queryset(...)` for **visibility only** (a hidden row is "not found", no existence leak — [Decision 10](#decision-10--permission-composition-update--delete-lookups-run-through-the-target-get_queryset)) — write authorization is the separate `permission_classes` layer ([Decision 15](#decision-15--write-authorization-a-drf-shaped-check_permission--metapermission_classes-seam)); `delete` fully materializes nested / connection-child relations before `delete()` in the same transaction (AR-M5); the post-write re-fetch keeps `select_related` / `prefetch_related` with **no** `.only(...)` deferral under the mutation operation ([`spec-035`][spec-035] G2 — [Decision 9](#decision-9--optimizer-composition-and-the-spec-035-g2-live-test-handoff)).
  - [ ] Package coverage: [`tests/mutations/test_resolvers.py`][test-mutations] + [`tests/mutations/test_fields.py`][test-mutations] + [`tests/mutations/test_permissions.py`][test-mutations] — create/update/delete happy paths, validation-error envelope (incl. `"__all__"` sentinel and the AR-H2 partial-constraint case), wrong-type `GlobalID` → `FieldError` (AR-H4), M2M replace/clear/omit (AR-M1), the `transaction.atomic` rollback (AR-M4), the write-auth seam (anonymous / model-perm denial vs allow, AR-H3), hidden-row not-found, and sync + async. The exact `only_fields` / `deferred_loading` plan state is pinned in the [`tests/optimizer/test_walker.py`][walker] mirror, not here, per this spec's own two-tier AR-M7 split ([`## Test plan`](#test-plan)).
- [ ] Slice 4: the products live write surface — **discharges the [`spec-035`][spec-035] G2 live-test handoff** (per [Decision 9](#decision-9--optimizer-composition-and-the-spec-035-g2-live-test-handoff))
  - [ ] `examples/fakeshop/apps/products/schema.py`: a `Mutation` type with `create_item` / `update_item` / `delete_item` (and at least one `Category` write) as `DjangoMutationField`s; `config/schema.py` wires `mutation=Mutation` into `DjangoSchema(...)` — a schema exposing generated mutations is built as `DjangoSchema`, never a plain `strawberry.Schema` ([Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async)).
  - [ ] [`test_products_api.py`][test-products-api] (each test seeded via `seed_data` / `create_users`): live `/graphql/` create / update / delete coverage, the validation-error envelope (incl. the AR-H2 partial-update collision on `unique_item_per_category`), **write authorization** (anonymous and missing-model-perm denial vs an authorized success, AR-H3), the visibility-scoped update/delete (a caller who cannot *see* a private row gets not-found), a wrong-type `GlobalID` → `FieldError` (AR-H4), and a `CaptureQueriesContext` assertion that a mutation response keeps `select_related` / `prefetch_related` with a bounded query count and no accidental lazy query — the [`spec-035`][spec-035] Slice 2 handoff discharged at the behavioral tier (exact `only_fields` state in the package mirror, AR-M7).
- [ ] Slice 5: doc updates + card-completion wrap (per [Doc updates](#doc-updates))
  - [ ] [`docs/GLOSSARY.md`][glossary] (promote [`DjangoMutation`][glossary-djangomutation] / [Input type generation][glossary-input-type-generation] / [`FieldError` envelope][glossary-fielderror-envelope] to `shipped (0.0.11)`, add the net-new `DjangoMutationField` **and `DjangoModelPermission` / write-auth** entries, pin the final public names — inputs / payload `node`·`result` slot / `FieldError` / `<field>_id` / `"__all__"` sentinel (AR test/doc correction), and append the G2-handoff-discharged note to the [`only()` projection][glossary-only-projection] entry), [`docs/README.md`][docs-readme] / [`README.md`][readme] (move mutations from "Coming next" to "Shipped today"), [`GOAL.md`][goal] (the DRF-migration mutation diff now references a shipped base), [`TODAY.md`][today] (products now demonstrates a write surface), [`CHANGELOG.md`][changelog] (only if the Slice 5 maintainer prompt explicitly requests it), [`KANBAN.md`][kanban] (card → Done via the kanban DB + re-render). **No version-file edits** ([Decision 13](#decision-13--version-bumps-are-owned-by-the-joint-0011-cut)).

## Problem statement

The package has no write side. Every shipped surface — [`DjangoType`][glossary-djangotype], the optimizer, [`FilterSet`][glossary-filterset] / [`OrderSet`][glossary-orderset], the Relay connection / node fields, the cascade permissions — is read-only. A consumer migrating from [`strawberry-graphql-django`][upstream-mutations] (which ships `create` / `update` / `delete`, custom mutations, and auto-generated `Input` / `PartialInput` types) or from `graphene-django` (which ships `DjangoModelFormMutation` / `SerializerMutation`) reaches the package and immediately hits a wall: there is no way to create, update, or delete a row through GraphQL. The card names this "the single largest unscoped gap against `strawberry-graphql-django`."

Three properties make the gap more than "add a resolver":

- **Input types must be generated, not hand-written.** A `Model.objects.create(...)` call needs an `Input` whose fields match the model's editable columns, with relations expressed as ids; the update path needs a `PartialInput` whose fields are all optional. Hand-declaring these per model re-introduces exactly the duplicate-field-definition burden the package exists to remove ([`GOAL.md`][goal] success-criterion 6: "no parallel field definitions"). They must derive from `Meta.model` and reuse the same scalar / relation converters the read side uses, so read and write share one wire contract.
- **Errors need a shared, typed envelope.** Validation failure must surface field-keyed messages, not a generic 500. graphene-django's `ErrorType` (a `field` name + a list of message strings) is the parity shape; the card mandates "one shared `errors: list[FieldError]` envelope across every flavor", reused unchanged by the form (`0.0.12`) and serializer / auth (`0.0.13`) cards. Defining it inconsistently now would fork the client contract across flavors forever.
- **The write side must compose with what already shipped.** A mutation that returns a queryset hits the optimizer ([`spec-035`][spec-035]'s **G2** gate exists *specifically because* this card makes that path mainstream); an `update` / `delete` must not mutate a row the target type's [`get_queryset`][glossary-get_queryset-visibility-hook] + [`apply_cascade_permissions`][glossary-apply_cascade_permissions] hide; the return / input target must resolve the model's **primary** [`DjangoType`][glossary-metaprimary]. None of these compositions exist yet, and getting any wrong bakes a correctness or security hole into the first write surface consumers touch.

This is a Required `strawberry-graphql-django` parity item (the card's own tag), foundational by the [`START.md`][start] "do both libraries provide it?" test — graphene-django and strawberry-graphql-django both ship mutations.

## Current state

A true description of the repo as this spec is authored:

- **No `mutations/` module, no write resolvers, no input generation as this spec is authored.** [`docs/TREE.md`][tree]'s *target* layout reserves `django_strawberry_framework/mutations/` and `tests/mutations/` for this card; neither exists on disk. The package root [`__init__.py`][init] exports no mutation symbol and `__all__` names none.
- **The set-family layout is the precedent.** [`filters/`][filters-sets] and [`orders/`][filters-sets] are each a four-module subpackage (`base.py` / `factories.py` / `inputs.py` / `sets.py`) with a metaclass-driven declarative class, a finalizer phase-2.5 binding pass ([`finalize_django_types`][glossary-finalize_django_types]), stable class-derived input names materialized as module globals before the schema is constructed, and a `tests/<subsystem>/` mirror. [`sets_mixins.py`][sets-mixins] hosts the lifecycle machinery shared across the FilterSet / OrderSet family; `mutations/` slots beside them.
- **The Meta-key machinery is stable and must not move.** [`types/base.py`][types-base] holds `DEFERRED_META_KEYS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"aggregate_class", "fields_class", "search_fields"})` and `ALLOWED_META_KEYS` beside it; a mutation does not add a `DjangoType` `Meta` key, so neither set changes ([Decision 12](#decision-12--finalization-seam-register-at-class-creation-bind-at-phase-25-no-deferred_meta_keys-change)).
- **The G2 gate is already in place and waiting for this card.** [`spec-035`][spec-035] shipped the operation-type `.only()` gate ([`walker.py::_enable_only_for_operation`][walker]) in `0.0.10`, explicitly "sequencing-critical *because of*" the `0.0.11` mutations cohort, and its Slice 2 test plan records a **mandatory live-test handoff**: "the first card that adds a fakeshop mutation returning a queryset **must** add a live `examples/fakeshop/test_query/` acceptance test proving the mutation queryset response keeps `select_related` / `prefetch_related` with no deferred loading." This card is that card; Slice 4 discharges the obligation.
- **The permission seam is shipped.** [`apply_cascade_permissions`][glossary-apply_cascade_permissions] ([`DONE-034-0.0.10`][kanban], [`permissions.py`][permissions]) and the [`get_queryset` visibility hook][glossary-get_queryset-visibility-hook] are live; the four products [`schema.py`][products-schema] types already call the cascade inside their hooks, so the products write surface inherits visibility scoping for free once `update` / `delete` route their lookups through `get_queryset` ([Decision 10](#decision-10--permission-composition-update--delete-lookups-run-through-the-target-get_queryset)).
- **`Meta.primary` resolution is shipped.** [`registry.py::TypeRegistry`][registry] resolves a model's primary type via `get(model)` / `primary_for(model)` ([`DONE-018-0.0.6`][kanban]); the mutation return / input target uses the same lookup auto-synthesized relation fields use.
- **The products write target is connections-only as this spec is authored.** [`products/schema.py`][products-schema]'s `Query` is four `DjangoConnectionField`s and there is **no** `Mutation` type; `config/schema.py` constructs a query-only schema with no `mutation=`. Slice 4 adds the `Mutation` type and wires it into a `DjangoSchema` (the constructor a generated mutation requires — [Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async)). The four models ([`Category`][products-models] / `Item` / `Property` / `Entry`) are editable Django models with FK relations and `UniqueConstraint`s — a realistic write surface (the `unique_item_per_category` constraint exercises the create error path); `Item` also carries the `attachment` [`Upload`][glossary-upload-scalar] file column the sibling `0.0.11` card maps.
- **The sibling `0.0.11` card supplies the file/image input mapping.** [`DONE-037-0.0.11`][kanban] ([`Upload` scalar][glossary-upload-scalar] + file/image mapping) maps `FileField` / `ImageField` to `Upload` on the input side this card generates, through the converter seam this card provides. The two share the `0.0.11` cut ([Decision 13](#decision-13--version-bumps-are-owned-by-the-joint-0011-cut)).

## Goals

1. **Ship the `DjangoMutation` base on the `class Meta` surface.** A consumer declares a mutation as a class with a nested `Meta` (`model` + `operation`), not a Strawberry decorator — the package's defining surface contract ([Decision 3](#decision-3--class-meta-surface-not-decorators-borrow-the-capabilities-reject-the-decorator-surface) / [Decision 5](#decision-5--public-surface-djangomutation-base--djangomutationfield-factory--fielderror-exported-from-the-root)).
2. **Auto-generate `Input` and `PartialInput`.** Derive both from `Meta.model`, honoring the relation-override contract from [`spec-010`][spec-010], with stable class-derived names and the read-side scalar / relation converters reused ([Decision 6](#decision-6--auto-generated-input--partialinput-types)).
3. **Define the shared `FieldError` envelope.** A public `FieldError` (`field`, `messages`, and the additive default-empty `codes` / `path`) plus the `errors: list[FieldError]` payload contract, returned unchanged by the `0.0.12` / `0.0.13` flavor cards ([Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper)).
4. **Ship `create` / `update` / `delete` resolvers, sync and async.** With `full_clean()` validation feeding the error envelope, and the optimizer re-fetching the post-write row for the response selection ([Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async)).
5. **Compose with the optimizer and discharge the G2 handoff.** The mutation re-fetch keeps `select_related` / `prefetch_related` and carries no `.only(...)` deferral under the mutation operation, proven by the live products SQL-shape test the [`spec-035`][spec-035] handoff mandates ([Decision 9](#decision-9--optimizer-composition-and-the-spec-035-g2-live-test-handoff)).
6. **Compose with permissions.** `update` / `delete` lookups run through the target type's `get_queryset` + cascade, so a hidden row is never mutable and never leaks its existence ([Decision 10](#decision-10--permission-composition-update--delete-lookups-run-through-the-target-get_queryset)).
7. **Ship the products live write surface.** Products gains a `Mutation` proving the whole pipeline end-to-end over `/graphql/` (Slice 4).
8. **Keep package version state owned by the joint `0.0.11` cut.** No slice edits `pyproject.toml`, `__version__`, [`tests/base/test_init.py::test_version`][test-base-init], or `uv.lock` ([Decision 13](#decision-13--version-bumps-are-owned-by-the-joint-0011-cut)).

## Non-goals

- **File / image upload inputs.** The [`Upload` scalar][glossary-upload-scalar] + `FileField` / `ImageField` mapping is the sibling `0.0.11` card ([`DONE-037-0.0.11`][kanban]); this card generates inputs for the shipped scalar / relation set through a per-field-type converter seam, and the sibling card supplies the `FileField` / `ImageField` → `Upload` mapping through it ([Out of scope](#out-of-scope-explicitly-tracked-elsewhere)).
- **Form-based mutations.** [`DjangoFormMutation`][glossary-djangoformmutation] / [`DjangoModelFormMutation`][glossary-djangomodelformmutation] (Django `Form` / `ModelForm` validation feeding the same envelope) are `0.0.12` ([Out of scope](#out-of-scope-explicitly-tracked-elsewhere)).
- **DRF serializer mutations and auth mutations.** [`SerializerMutation`][glossary-serializermutation] (`Meta.serializer_class`, `lookup_field`, `model_operations`) and [Auth mutations][glossary-auth-mutations] (`login` / `logout` / `register`) are `0.0.13`; this card freezes the `FieldError` envelope they consume but ships neither.
- **Relay `clientMutationId` / single-input-mutation wrapping.** graphene-django's `ClientIDMutation` `clientMutationId` round-trip and strawberry-django's `input_mutation` single-`input`-argument shape are not adopted in `0.0.11` ([Decision 14](#decision-14--single-data-argument-no-relay-clientmutationid-in-0011)).
- **Bulk / batch mutations, nested writes, and `full_clean` opt-out granularity.** Upstream's nested-object create (`ParsedObject` / `ParsedObjectList`) and `FullCleanOptions` are out; `0.0.11` writes one root model with relations expressed as existing ids ([Out of scope](#out-of-scope-explicitly-tracked-elsewhere)).
- **A new `DjangoType` `Meta` key or settings key.** The mutation `Meta` is the mutation class's own namespace; no `DjangoType` `Meta` key and no `DJANGO_STRAWBERRY_FRAMEWORK` entry is added ([`AGENTS.md`][agents] #"Add a settings key only when the feature that needs it lands").
- **A version bump.** Owned by the joint `0.0.11` cut ([Decision 13](#decision-13--version-bumps-are-owned-by-the-joint-0011-cut)).

## Borrowing posture

Per the [`START.md`][start] "do both libraries provide it? → foundational" test, mutations are **Required `strawberry-graphql-django` parity** (the card's own 🍓 Required tag) and graphene-django provides them too. The borrowing splits cleanly along the package's standing line — *behaviorally* copy `strawberry-graphql-django`'s good ideas; *surface-wise* copy `django-graphene-filters` / DRF (`class Meta`). The runtime capabilities (create / update / delete, auto-generated `Input` / `PartialInput`, the `handle_django_errors` → typed-error path, optimizer-composed return value) are adopted at the **outcome** level from strawberry-django; the consumer-facing **shape** (a base class with a nested `Meta`, a field factory on the schema's `Mutation` type, the `ErrorType`-shaped `FieldError`) is the graphene-django / DRF surface. The decorator / field-verb mechanism strawberry-django uses (`@strawberry_django.input`, `create()` / `update()` / `delete()`) is **explicitly rejected** — it is the exact API the package exists to replace.

### Reference-package parity checkpoint

| Upstream | `django-strawberry-framework` | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`strawberry_django.create` / `update` / `delete`][upstream-mutations] field-verb factories + `@strawberry_django.input` decorators | `DjangoMutation` base + `Meta.operation` selector + `DjangoMutationField` factory ([Decision 3](#decision-3--class-meta-surface-not-decorators-borrow-the-capabilities-reject-the-decorator-surface) / [Decision 5](#decision-5--public-surface-djangomutation-base--djangomutationfield-factory--fielderror-exported-from-the-root)) | this card — borrow the operations, reject the decorator surface |
| [strawberry-django auto-generated `Input` / `PartialInput`][upstream-mutations] from a model | generated `<Model>Input` / `<Model>PartialInput` from `Meta.model`, read-side converters reused ([Decision 6](#decision-6--auto-generated-input--partialinput-types)) | this card — required parity |
| [graphene-django `ErrorType`][graphene-rest-mutation] (`field: String!` + `messages: [String!]!`) on the mutation payload | public `FieldError` (`field`, `messages: list[str]`, plus the additive `codes` / `path`), `errors: list[FieldError]` on the `<Name>Payload` ([Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper)) | this card — the `ErrorType` parity core, defined here and shared by every flavor |
| [strawberry-django `handle_django_errors` → `Type \| OperationInfo` union][upstream-mutations] | payload wrapper carrying object + `errors` (graphene-django shape), not a disjoint union ([Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper)) | borrow the error-capture outcome, not the union surface |
| [strawberry-django `full_clean` validation + optimizer-composed return][upstream-mutations] | `full_clean()` feeding the envelope; post-write re-fetch through [`DjangoOptimizerExtension`][glossary-djangooptimizerextension] under the G2 mutation gate ([Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async) / [Decision 9](#decision-9--optimizer-composition-and-the-spec-035-g2-live-test-handoff)) | this card — required parity |
| [graphene-django `DjangoModelFormMutation` / `SerializerMutation`][graphene-rest-mutation] `Meta`-driven flavors | the same `DjangoMutation` base + `Meta`; the form (`0.0.12`) and serializer (`0.0.13`) flavors subclass it | deferred (flavor cards) — the base ships here |
| graphene-django `ClientIDMutation` `clientMutationId` round-trip | not adopted ([Decision 14](#decision-14--single-data-argument-no-relay-clientmutationid-in-0011)) | deliberate non-adoption |

### From `strawberry-graphql-django` — borrow the runtime, not the surface

- **Operations.** `create` / `update` / `delete` as the three foundational operations, each with model-derived input and a `full_clean()` validation pass — adopted; the field-verb factories that spell them are not.
- **Input generation.** Model → `Input` (required) / `PartialInput` (optional) with relations as ids — adopted; strawberry-django's nested-object `ParsedObject` / `ParsedObjectList` (nested create/connect/disconnect) is deferred ([Out of scope](#out-of-scope-explicitly-tracked-elsewhere)).
- **Optimizer-composed return.** The post-write row is re-fetched and optimizer-planned for the response selection — adopted, and refined by the package's own G2 gate so the mutation re-fetch never carries a `.only(...)` deferral ([Decision 9](#decision-9--optimizer-composition-and-the-spec-035-g2-live-test-handoff)).

### From `graphene-django` / DRF — borrow the user-facing shape

- **The `class Meta` declaration.** A `DjangoMutation` subclass with a nested `Meta`, parallel to `DjangoModelFormMutation` / `SerializerMutation`; the DRF / `django-graphene-filters` shape every other consumer surface in the package already uses.
- **The `ErrorType` envelope.** `FieldError` is graphene-django's `ErrorType` (a `field` name + a list of message strings), the shape the card pins for cross-flavor reuse.

### Explicitly do not borrow

- **The decorator / field-verb surface** (`@strawberry_django.input`, `create()` / `update()` / `delete()`) — the exact API [`START.md`][start] names as "the explicit reason this package exists"; the `class Meta` base class replaces it.
- **The disjoint `Type | OperationInfo` union return** — rejected for the graphene-django payload-with-`errors` shape the card's `FieldError` parity implies ([Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper)).
- **The Graphene runtime** (`ClientIDMutation`, `clientMutationId`, relay-mutation argument wrapping) — Strawberry stays the engine; the Relay mutation conventions are not adopted in `0.0.11` ([Decision 14](#decision-14--single-data-argument-no-relay-clientmutationid-in-0011)).

## User-facing API

One new base class, one new field factory, and one new public payload type — no new `DjangoType` `Meta` key, no constructor argument on existing surfaces. The canonical consumer surface declares the mutation with a nested `Meta` and exposes it on the schema's `Mutation` type through the factory, mirroring the read-side `DjangoConnectionField` idiom:

```python
import strawberry

from django_strawberry_framework import DjangoMutation, DjangoMutationField

from . import models
from .schema import ItemType  # the model's primary DjangoType


class CreateItem(DjangoMutation):
    class Meta:
        model = models.Item
        operation = "create"


class UpdateItem(DjangoMutation):
    class Meta:
        model = models.Item
        operation = "update"


class DeleteItem(DjangoMutation):
    class Meta:
        model = models.Item
        operation = "delete"


@strawberry.type
class Mutation:
    # No class-attribute annotation: the return payload is generated at
    # finalization and cannot be named at import, so the factory types the
    # field itself via a `strawberry.lazy` forward-ref (Decision 7).
    create_item = DjangoMutationField(CreateItem)
    update_item = DjangoMutationField(UpdateItem)
    delete_item = DjangoMutationField(DeleteItem)
```

The generated schema fields are:

```graphql
type Mutation {
  createItem(data: ItemInput!): CreateItemPayload!
  updateItem(id: ID!, data: ItemPartialInput!): UpdateItemPayload!
  deleteItem(id: ID!): DeleteItemPayload!
}

input ItemInput {
  name: String!
  description: String
  categoryId: GlobalID!
  isPrivate: Boolean
  attachment: Upload
}

input ItemPartialInput {
  name: String
  description: String
  categoryId: GlobalID
  isPrivate: Boolean
  attachment: Upload
}

type FieldError {
  field: String!
  messages: [String!]!
  codes: [String!]!
  path: [String!]!
}

type CreateItemPayload {
  node: ItemType
  errors: [FieldError!]!
}
```

`ItemInput` carries the model's **editable** columns with each field required **only when it has no usable default** — no Django `default`, not `null=True`, and (for text fields) not `blank=True` — so `name` / `categoryId` are required while `description` (`blank=True, default=""`), `isPrivate` (`default=False`), and the `attachment` file column (`null=True, blank=True`, mapped to the [`Upload` scalar][glossary-upload-scalar] by the sibling `0.0.11` card) are optional even in the create input (the DRF `required=False`-from-`default`/`blank`/`null` rule, [Decision 6](#decision-6--auto-generated-input--partialinput-types)). `ItemPartialInput` carries them all optional (the `update` shape). The forward FK `category` becomes `categoryId: GlobalID!` (the target's id type — `GlobalID` because `ItemType` is Relay-Node-shaped, the raw pk scalar otherwise). The `Mutation` field is assigned with **no** class-attribute annotation (`create_item = DjangoMutationField(CreateItem)`); the factory types it from the generated `<Name>Payload` via a `strawberry.lazy` forward-ref ([Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper)). On success the payload's `node` (the uniform object slot — `node` for a Relay-Node target, `result` otherwise; never a model-derived name, [Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper)) is the optimizer-re-fetched object and `errors` is empty; on a `full_clean()` failure `node` is `null` and `errors` carries one `FieldError` per offending field. `update` / `delete` resolve the row through `ItemType.get_queryset(...)`, so a row the caller cannot see is "not found" (a single `FieldError` on the `id` field), never an existence leak. The root `id:` argument renders **`ID!`**, not `GlobalID!` — the `node(id: ID!)` Relay-spec signature the shipped `DjangoNodeField` uses (the package decodes the GlobalID server-side); the resolver decodes it and type-checks the decoded model against the mutation target, returning a `FieldError` on `id` for a malformed / unresolvable / wrong-model id rather than coercing it to a bare pk. A **relation** id (`categoryId`, M2M lists) is type-checked against its target model AND resolved through that target's visibility `get_queryset`, so a relation id for a row the caller cannot see is a `FieldError` on that relation field — a permitted writer can never attach a row they could not see. **Write authorization is a separate contract from visibility:** all three operations run `Meta.permission_classes` (default `DjangoModelPermission` — the Django `add` / `change` / `delete` model perms), so an unauthorized or anonymous caller is denied before any write ([Decision 15](#decision-15--write-authorization-a-drf-shaped-check_permission--metapermission_classes-seam)); `get_queryset` scopes which rows are *visible*, not whether they may be *written*. The async surface is automatic — a `DjangoMutationField` over an async-context schema awaits the same pipeline.

Supplying a hand-written input instead of the generated one:

```python
class CreateItem(DjangoMutation):
    class Meta:
        model = models.Item
        operation = "create"
        input_class = MyHandWrittenItemInput   # overrides specific generated fields; the generator fills the rest
```

### Error shapes

- A `Meta` from which **no model can be resolved** (in `0.0.11`, a missing `Meta.model` — the `0.0.12` / `0.0.13` flavor cards supply it via `form_class` / `serializer_class` through the `_resolve_model` seam, [Decision 5](#decision-5--public-surface-djangomutation-base--djangomutationfield-factory--fielderror-exported-from-the-root)), naming an `operation` not in `{"create", "update", "delete"}`, carrying an unknown `Meta` key, or referencing an `input_class` / `partial_input_class` that is not a `@strawberry.input`-decorated type raises [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] at mutation-class creation, naming the offending key.
- A `DjangoMutation` over a model with no registered (or no **primary**) [`DjangoType`][glossary-djangotype] raises [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] at [`finalize_django_types`][glossary-finalize_django_types] (the return type and input target cannot be resolved) — the same finalize-time fail-loud the relation finalizer uses ([Decision 11](#decision-11--primary-type-resolution-return-type-and-input-target-resolve-the-models-primary-djangotype)).
- Two **distinct** generated input or payload shapes that would resolve to the same schema-global GraphQL name raise [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] at [`finalize_django_types`][glossary-finalize_django_types], naming both mutations (AR-M6) — identical shapes dedupe and share one type ([Decision 6](#decision-6--auto-generated-input--partialinput-types) / [Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper)).
- A model `ValidationError` from `full_clean()` — including a `UniqueConstraint` violation, which `validate_constraints()` catches before `save()` (Major-2) — is **not** an exception at the GraphQL boundary; it populates `errors: list[FieldError]` and returns the payload with a null object (a multi-field-constraint error keys to the `"__all__"` sentinel, AR-M3). A concurrent-race `IntegrityError` at `save()` maps to the same envelope as a documented best-effort fallback ([Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async)).
- A relation `<field>_id` that is a well-formed `GlobalID` for the **wrong** target model (an `Item` id passed to `categoryId`) is a `FieldError` on that relation field — never coerced to a raw pk and looked up cross-model, never a raw `DoesNotExist` (AR-H4, [Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async) step 1).
- A write the caller is **not authorized** to perform (`Meta.permission_classes` / `check_permission` denial — by default a missing Django `add` / `change` / `delete` model perm, or an anonymous caller) raises a `GraphQLError` in the response's top-level `errors`, **not** a field-keyed [`FieldError` envelope][glossary-fielderror-envelope] entry ([Decision 15](#decision-15--write-authorization-a-drf-shaped-check_permission--metapermission_classes-seam)).
- A generated mutation reached through a plain `strawberry.Schema` instead of `DjangoSchema` raises [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] naming the mutation class, **before any database work** — the write transaction has to span GraphQL response completion and only the `DjangoSchema` execution context opens it ([Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async)).
- A sync mutation resolver whose target type has an `async def get_queryset` raises [`SyncMisuseError`][glossary-syncmisuseerror] (coroutine closed first, no `RuntimeWarning`), pointing the consumer at an async schema or a sync hook — the same discipline the Relay node defaults and [`apply_cascade_permissions`][glossary-apply_cascade_permissions] follow ([Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async)).

## Architectural decisions

### Decision 1 — Spec filename and canonical naming

The spec file lives at **`docs/SPECS/spec-036-mutations-0_0_11.md`** (this document).

Rationale companion — this Decision's justification and its two rejected alternatives: [Decision 1][rationale-d1].

### Decision 2 — Card-scope boundary: the mutation foundation ships; the flavor cards and uploads are out; the `FieldError` envelope is defined here

This card ships the **model-driven mutation foundation** end-to-end: the [`DjangoMutation`][glossary-djangomutation] base, [auto-generated `Input` / `PartialInput`][glossary-input-type-generation], `create` / `update` / `delete` resolvers (sync + async), the [`FieldError` envelope][glossary-fielderror-envelope], optimizer + permission composition, and the products live write surface. It explicitly does **not** ship the adjacent flavors, each owned by a named card:

- **Uploads** ([`Upload` scalar][glossary-upload-scalar], [`DjangoFileType`][glossary-djangofiletype] / [`DjangoImageType`][glossary-djangoimagetype]) — the sibling `0.0.11` card [`DONE-037-0.0.11`][kanban]. This card provides the input-converter seam (a per-field-type input mapping) and 037 plugs `Upload` into it without re-opening the generator, so a `FileField` / `ImageField` editable column reaches the generated input as an `Upload` scalar field.
- **Form-based mutations** ([`DjangoFormMutation`][glossary-djangoformmutation] / [`DjangoModelFormMutation`][glossary-djangomodelformmutation]) — `0.0.12`.
- **DRF serializer + auth mutations** ([`SerializerMutation`][glossary-serializermutation], [Auth mutations][glossary-auth-mutations]) — `0.0.13`.

The **`FieldError` envelope is defined in this card and shared, not re-declared, by the downstream flavor cohorts** — the form-based (`0.0.12`) and DRF-serializer / auth (`0.0.13`) cards (the [`Upload` scalar][glossary-upload-scalar] sibling `0.0.11` card does **not** touch the envelope) — mirroring [`spec-034`][spec-034] Decision 2's "define the surface here, implement the rest later" move (there: the per-field read gate signature was pinned in `0.0.10` and implemented with `FieldSet` in `0.1.1`). The card DoD makes the reuse explicit ("reused unchanged by `TODO-ALPHA-039-0.0.13`, `TODO-ALPHA-038-0.0.12`"). Exactly one `FieldError` class exists package-wide and every flavor imports it, which is what makes the client contract one instead of three; the type is **not** frozen against growth — a flavor may extend it only with an **additive, default-empty** field, which is exactly what `codes` and `path` are ([Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper)), and may never change or remove an existing one.

Rationale companion — this Decision's justification and its two rejected alternatives: [Decision 2][rationale-d2].

### Decision 3 — `class Meta` surface, not decorators: borrow the capabilities, reject the decorator surface

A `DjangoMutation` is a **base class with a nested `class Meta`**, declared and exposed exactly like every other consumer surface in the package. It is **not** a Strawberry / strawberry-django decorator (`@strawberry_django.input`, `create()` / `update()` / `delete()` field verbs).

Rationale companion — this Decision's justification and its two rejected alternatives: [Decision 3][rationale-d3].

### Decision 4 — Module and test locations: `mutations/` subpackage mirroring `filters/` / `orders/`

- **Source:** `django_strawberry_framework/mutations/` — the subpackage directory [`docs/TREE.md`][tree]'s target layout reserves, split in the spirit of the [`filters/`][filters-sets] / [`orders/`][filters-sets] subpackages (a declarative-set shape, though the module names differ — `inputs` / `sets` / `resolvers` / `fields` / `permissions` here vs. `base` / `factories` / `inputs` / `sets` there; TREE reserves only the `mutations/` directory, and the split is the set-family precedent, not a TREE enumeration): [`inputs.py`][mutations-inputs] (input + payload + `FieldError` generation), [`sets.py`][mutations-sets] (`DjangoMutation` + metaclass + `Meta` validation + finalizer binding), [`resolvers.py`][mutations-resolvers] (the sync + async write pipeline), [`fields.py`][mutations-fields] (`DjangoMutationField`), and [`permissions.py`][mutations-permissions] (`DjangoModelPermission` + the shared permission-class walk, [Decision 15](#decision-15--write-authorization-a-drf-shaped-check_permission--metapermission_classes-seam)); [`mutations/operations.py`][mutations-operations] holds the canonical operation-descriptor vocabulary the flavors share. The mutation subsystem does **not** ride [`sets_mixins.py`][sets-mixins], whose machinery is `RelatedFilter` / `RelatedOrder`-shaped; the write-flavor lifecycle substrate the `038` / `039` flavors share (the declaration registry, the `Meta`-validating metaclass factory, the resolver seams, the shape-build cache) lives in [`sets.py`][mutations-sets] itself and in [`utils/inputs.py`][utils-inputs].
- **Tests:** new [`tests/mutations/`][test-mutations] mirroring the source modules (`test_inputs.py` / `test_sets.py` / `test_resolvers.py` / `test_fields.py` / `test_permissions.py`), per the one-to-one rule; the tree also carries `test_operations.py` and `test_write_transaction.py`, mirroring modules other cards own; composition pins that belong to other surfaces extend those surfaces' files ([`tests/optimizer/test_walker.py`][walker] for the G2 plan-shape); the lookup-scoping pin is [`tests/mutations/test_resolvers.py`][test-mutations]`::test_hidden_row_update_is_not_found_no_existence_leak` plus [`tests/mutations/test_permissions.py`][test-mutations]`::test_hidden_row_is_not_found_before_auth_signal_no_existence_leak`; live coverage extends [`test_products_api.py`][test-products-api].

Rationale companion — this Decision's justification and its two rejected alternatives: [Decision 4][rationale-d4].

### Decision 5 — Public surface: `DjangoMutation` base + `DjangoMutationField` factory + `FieldError`, exported from the root

Four net-new public symbols, re-exported from [`django_strawberry_framework/__init__.py`][init] and added to `__all__`:

- `DjangoMutation` — the base class.
- `DjangoMutationField` — the field factory that exposes a mutation on the schema's `Mutation` type, the write-side sibling of [`DjangoConnectionField`][glossary-djangoconnectionfield] / [`DjangoListField`][glossary-djangolistfield] / [`DjangoNodeField`][glossary-djangonodefield] (all factories assigned to class attributes on an `@strawberry.type`). Unlike those read-side factories — which read the consumer's class-attribute annotation for the field type — `DjangoMutationField` is assigned **without** an annotation (`create_item = DjangoMutationField(CreateItem)`) and types the field itself from the generated `<Name>Payload` via a `strawberry.lazy` forward-ref; an eager `create_item: CreateItem.Payload` annotation cannot exist at import (see [Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper)).
- `FieldError` — the public `@strawberry.type` (`field: str`, `messages: list[str]`, `codes: list[str]`, `path: list[str]`) consumers reference in the payload contract.
- `DjangoModelPermission` — the default write-authorization permission class (and documented base for custom permission classes) consumers pass to `Meta.permission_classes` ([Decision 15](#decision-15--write-authorization-a-drf-shaped-check_permission--metapermission_classes-seam)).

The operation is selected by `Meta.operation` ∈ `{"create", "update", "delete"}` (a single string key — the vocabulary the operation descriptors in [`mutations/operations.py`][mutations-operations] derive), not a separate base class per operation. Write authorization is a separate, DRF-shaped contract — `Meta.permission_classes` (default `[DjangoModelPermission]`) and an overridable `check_permission(self, info, operation, data, instance=None)` method — that runs alongside the operation pipeline ([Decision 15](#decision-15--write-authorization-a-drf-shaped-check_permission--metapermission_classes-seam)); it is the mutation's own `Meta`/method namespace, not a `DjangoType` `Meta` key.

**Model resolution is a forward-compat seam (Medium-5).** The base metaclass does not hard-require the literal `Meta.model` attribute; it requires a *resolvable* model and raises [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] only when none can be found, through an overridable `_resolve_model(meta)` step. In `0.0.11` the sole source is `Meta.model`, so `model` is required in practice — but routing it through `_resolve_model` lets the `0.0.12` form flavor derive the model from `Meta.form_class._meta.model` and the `0.0.13` serializer flavor from `Meta.serializer_class.Meta.model` (exactly how [`GOAL.md`][goal]'s `class CreateCategory(DjangoMutation): class Meta: serializer_class = CategorySerializer` declares a mutation **without** a `Meta.model`) without re-opening the base validation. This freezes the `Meta`-validation contract for the flavor subclasses just as [Decision 7](#decision-7--the-shared-fielderror-envelope-and-the-payload-wrapper) freezes the `FieldError` envelope for them — so `038` / `039` inherit a base that does not paint them into a corner.

Rationale companion — this Decision's justification and its three rejected alternatives: [Decision 5][rationale-d5].

### Decision 6 — Auto-generated `Input` / `PartialInput` types

[`mutations/inputs.py`][mutations-inputs] generates two input types per mutation from the **editable fields of `Meta.model`** — *not* the read-side [`DjangoType`][glossary-djangotype] field selection (see the field-set rule below; the return *type* still resolves the primary `DjangoType`, [Decision 11](#decision-11--primary-type-resolution-return-type-and-input-target-resolve-the-models-primary-djangotype)):

- **`<Model>Input`** — every editable field, each **required only when it has no usable default** (Major-1): no Django `default`, `null=False`, and (for text / char fields) `blank=False`; otherwise the field is **optional** with a `strawberry.UNSET` default. This is DRF's `required=False`-from-`default`/`blank`/`null` rule, and it matches `Model.objects.create(...)` semantics (Django supplies the omitted columns). So a `NOT NULL`, no-default, non-blank column like `name` (and a non-null FK like `category`) is required, while `description` (`blank=True, default=""`) and `is_private` (`default=False`) are optional — the headline `ItemInput` above. **An M2M field is *always* optional even in the create input** (the per-field required rule does not apply to it): a forward `ManyToManyField` reports `null=False, blank=False, has_default()=False` (so the literal rule would mark it required), but a parent row cannot carry M2M rows until it has a pk, and the resolver's replace-on-provide / clear-on-empty / unchanged-on-omit contract ([Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async) step 5, AR-M1) needs the M2M input to be omittable — so M2M defaults to `strawberry.UNSET` in both the create and the partial input. (A blanket "every editable field required" rule was rejected: it would force `description` / `isPrivate` required on products *and* on [`GOAL.md`][goal]'s north-star `Galaxy` / `CelestialBody` models, which share the identical `blank=True, default=""` / `default=False` shape, diverging from DRF and strawberry-django.)
- **`<Model>PartialInput`** — every editable field optional, defaulting to `strawberry.UNSET` (matches `Model.objects.update(...)`); only the provided fields are written.

**Field set (Medium-4 — derived from editable *model* fields, not the read selection).** The input fields are the model's editable, settable columns: exclude the auto pk, non-`editable` columns (`auto_now` / `auto_now_add` timestamps and any `editable=False` field), and reverse relations — then optionally narrow by the mutation's own `Meta.fields` / `Meta.exclude` ([Decision 5](#decision-5--public-surface-djangomutation-base--djangomutationfield-factory--fielderror-exported-from-the-root)). The set is **not** the read-side `DjangoType` selection, which resolves the read/write mismatch in both directions: a read type's `fields = "__all__"` includes read-only `created_date` / `updated_date` that must never be writable (so they are excluded from the input), and an editable column a read type *omits* for permissions (the cookbook `ValueNode` deliberately hides `description`) is still a writable model column (so it *is* exposed on the input). To keep an editable column off the write surface, the consumer names it in the mutation's `Meta.exclude` — explicitly, not as a side effect of the read selection. Map scalars through the **same** [scalar][glossary-scalar-field-conversion] / [choice-enum][glossary-choice-enum-generation] / [specialized-scalar][glossary-specialized-scalar-conversions] converters the read side uses (so read and write share one wire contract); map a forward FK / OneToOne to a single `<field>_id` input typed as the target's id (`GlobalID` for a Relay-Node target, the raw pk scalar otherwise) — a `GlobalID` is **type-checked against the relation target** at decode, never coerced cross-model ([Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async) step 1, AR-H4); map an M2M to `list[<id>]` (replace-set write semantics, [Decision 8](#decision-8--resolver-pipeline-decode--full_clean--write--optimizer-re-fetch--payload-sync-and-async) step 5, AR-M1).

**Type identity and naming (AR-H1 / AR-M6).** A generated input type's identity is its **complete shape** — `(model, operation kind, frozenset(effective field names))` — not the model alone, because GraphQL type names are schema-global. The stable model-derived names `<Model>Input` / `<Model>PartialInput` are reserved for the **canonical full editable shape**: two mutations that both take the full shape resolve to that one materialized module global (Apollo-cache-friendly, exactly the [`FilterSet`][glossary-filterset] / [`OrderSet`][glossary-orderset] input-naming property). A mutation that **narrows** the shape via `Meta.fields` / `Meta.exclude` gets a **deterministic shape-derived name** (the model name plus an operation- / field-set-derived suffix) so a narrowed input never silently claims the bare `<Model>Input` name and can neither leak a field one mutation meant to exclude nor make another mutation too narrow; two narrowings to the *same* effective shape still dedupe to one type. If two **distinct** shapes would resolve to the same generated GraphQL name, finalization raises [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] naming both mutations (the early-config-error posture, not silent schema drift — AR-M6).

**Custom inputs follow the generated field-naming scheme (AR-M2).** `Meta.input_class` / `Meta.partial_input_class` override **specific** generated fields with a hand-written `@strawberry.input` and the generator **merges** in the rest of the editable shape — the **relation-override contract** from [`spec-010`][spec-010] (a consumer-authored input field is honored, not clobbered; the consumer need only declare the field(s) it customizes, not re-list the whole shape) — but in `0.0.11` a custom input must use the **same field-naming scheme the generator emits**: scalar attribute names equal to the model field names, forward FK / OneToOne as `<field>_id`, M2M as `list[<id>]`. That deterministic naming is what lets the resolver map input attributes back onto model fields / relations with no per-field mapping declaration; a custom input whose field names diverge from this scheme is out of scope for `0.0.11` (the resolver has no contract to apply it safely — restrict to the generated scheme, or wait for an explicit mapping API). **A relation override is type-locked as well as name-locked.** A custom input may not re-declare a generated relation field with a different id shape: the override must keep the generated core type (a Relay [`GlobalID`][glossary-djangotype] target stays `GlobalID`, a raw-pk target stays the raw pk scalar) **and** its container shape (a scalar for FK / OneToOne, a one-level `list` for M2M), else the mutation raises [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] at class creation. This is a boundary, not polish: re-declaring `category_id` as a raw `int` when the generated shape is `GlobalID` would route the value down the raw-pk path and past the relation type-check and visibility confirmation, which is exactly how the [`## User-facing API`](#user-facing-api) guarantee that a permitted writer can never attach a row they could not see would be bypassed. **File / image columns take the override skip like any other scalar:** a `FileField` / `ImageField` maps to the [`Upload` scalar][glossary-upload-scalar] as a scalar-kind input (its input attribute is the plain field name, never `<field>_id`) and rides the same override-skip, requiredness, and nullability tail; it is removed from the write surface via `Meta.exclude` like any other column.

Rationale companion — this Decision's justification and its three rejected alternatives: [Decision 6][rationale-d6].

### Decision 7 — The shared `FieldError` envelope and the payload wrapper

The error contract is a public `FieldError` `@strawberry.type` — `field: str` and `messages: list[str]` are graphene-django's `ErrorType` parity core, and `codes: list[str]` / `path: list[str]` are additive, default-empty lists that let a client branch without parsing localized message text or the dotted `field` string (`codes` carries the structured codes — a DRF `ErrorDetail.code`, a Django `ValidationError.code`, or a framework code such as `invalid` / `null` / `not_found` / `constraint`; `path` is the `field` string split into segments, so a **root** non-field error is `field="__all__"` with an **empty** `path` while a **nested** one keeps its segments). The type is surfaced through a generated per-mutation `<Name>Payload` carrying the mutated object (nullable) **and** `errors: list[FieldError]!`. On success `errors` is empty and the object is set; on validation failure the object is `null` and `errors` carries one entry per offending field — the model's `NON_FIELD_ERRORS` bucket (and any constraint- or `clean()`-level error not tied to a single field) maps to a `FieldError` whose `field` is the **`"__all__"` sentinel** (Django's own `NON_FIELD_ERRORS` value, AR-M3), used consistently for every model-level / multi-field-constraint error so the sentinel is a stable, documented part of the public contract rather than an ad-hoc empty string.

**Payload object field name — uniform, never model-derived (AR-H5).** The payload's object field is **not** named off the model (which would collide with Python / GraphQL constraints for names like `Property` → `property`, and with future payload-metadata fields). It is a **uniform slot**: `node` when the target's primary [`DjangoType`][glossary-djangotype] is `relay.Node`-shaped (the package's Relay convention — `CreateItemPayload { node: ItemType, errors }`), and `result` for a non-Node target (`CreateThingPayload { result: ThingType, errors }`). For the products write surface every primary type is Node-shaped, so the pinned payload fields are `node` on `CreateItemPayload` / `UpdateItemPayload` / `DeleteItemPayload` and identically for `Category` and `Property` — **no `property`-named field is ever generated**.

**Where the envelope is constructed.** The `FieldError` type is defined in [`mutations/inputs.py`][mutations-inputs], while the constructors that build one — the `ValidationError` → envelope mapping, the `"__all__"` keying, the relation and integrity-error builders, and the error-path join — are the flavor-neutral [`utils/errors.py`][utils-errors], so the form, serializer, and auth flavors populate the same envelope through the same code rather than re-deriving it.

**Payload type-name collisions (AR-M6).** Generated `<Name>Payload` names are schema-global like the input names; if two mutations (e.g. same class name in different modules) would generate the same `<Name>Payload` for distinct shapes, finalization raises [`ConfigurationError`][glossary-configurationerror] naming both — the same early-error posture [Decision 6](#decision-6--auto-generated-input--partialinput-types) takes for inputs, never silent schema drift.

**Payload exposure timing (resolves Major-3 — the import-time hazard).** The `<Name>Payload` is materialized at [`finalize_django_types`][glossary-finalize_django_types] phase 2.5 ([Decision 12](#decision-12--finalization-seam-register-at-class-creation-bind-at-phase-25-no-deferred_meta_keys-change)), *after* `@strawberry.type class Mutation` has already evaluated its field annotations at import. So an eager `create_item: CreateItem.Payload = DjangoMutationField(CreateItem)` annotation cannot work — `CreateItem.Payload` is not a concrete attribute at import and raises `AttributeError` (unlike `DjangoConnection[CategoryType]`, which names a class that already exists). Resolution: `DjangoMutationField` is assigned with **no** class-attribute annotation and types the field from the bound payload via a `strawberry.lazy("django_strawberry_framework.mutations.inputs")` forward-ref on its synthesized resolver's return annotation — resolved at schema build, after finalize has materialized `<Name>Payload`. The consumer writes `create_item = DjangoMutationField(CreateItem)` (see the [User-facing API](#user-facing-api)); there is no `.field()`-classmethod form on the mutation base.

Rationale companion — this Decision's justification and its two rejected alternatives: [Decision 7][rationale-d7].

### Decision 8 — Resolver pipeline: decode → `full_clean()` → write → optimizer re-fetch → payload (sync and async)

[`mutations/resolvers.py`][mutations-resolvers] runs one pipeline per operation, in both sync and async forms (the form chosen **at runtime**, per call, via `in_async_context()` — the same runtime dispatch [`DjangoListField`][glossary-djangolistfield]'s default generated resolver uses. `DjangoListField`'s other half, the construction-time `is_async_callable` inspection of a *consumer* resolver, has no counterpart here: the mutation pipeline is package-owned and `DjangoMutationField` exposes no `resolver=` seam to inspect):

1. **Decode** the `data:` input (and `id:` for update / delete) — `GlobalID` / pk decode for relations, `UNSET` stripping for partial input. **Relation `GlobalID` decode enforces the target type (AR-H4):** when a `<field>_id` is a `GlobalID`, its decoded `type_name` must resolve to the relation's Django target model; a well-formed id for the *wrong* model (an `Item` `GlobalID` passed to `categoryId`) is a `FieldError` on that relation field, **never** stripped to a raw pk and looked up cross-model against `Category` (even if the numeric pks collide), and never a raw `DoesNotExist`. The decode primitives themselves — the relation type-check, the visibility confirmation of a decoded relation set, the scalar-leaf decode, and the `UNSET` strip — are the flavor-neutral [`utils/write_values.py`][utils-write-values] and [`utils/inputs.py`][utils-inputs], shared with the form and serializer flavors.
2. **Locate** (update / delete): resolve the row through the target type's `get_queryset(...)` ([Decision 10](#decision-10--permission-composition-update--delete-lookups-run-through-the-target-get_queryset)); a miss returns a not-found `FieldError` on `id`.
3. **Authorize** (AR-H3, [Decision 15](#decision-15--write-authorization-a-drf-shaped-check_permission--metapermission_classes-seam)): run `check_permission` / `Meta.permission_classes`. For `create` this runs **before** step 4 with `instance=None`; for `update` / `delete` it runs **after** the step-2 visibility lookup with the located `instance` (so object-level checks see it, and a row the caller cannot see is already not-found before any authorization signal). A denial **raises** a `GraphQLError` (top-level `errors`), distinct from the validation envelope.
4. **Validate**: build (create) or update the instance and call `full_clean()`. `exclude` is the set of fields the input did not provide **minus any unprovided field that co-participates in a `UniqueConstraint` / `unique_together` / `unique` check with a *provided* field (AR-H2)**, and it is computed for **both** operations: on `update` an unsent column keeps its stored value and is not re-validated; on `create` an unprovided column is left to its model default rather than validated against the empty value the unfilled instance carries (mirroring `Model.objects.create()`). So changing only `Item.name` still validates the `unique_item_per_category` constraint against the instance's current DB `category` (the loaded row supplies the unchanged members), while a genuinely unrelated unsent field stays excluded (DRF `partial=True` parity — an unsent, unconstrained field never raises a spurious `FieldError`). Because the update path loads the existing row (step 2), the instance is already filled with current database values; `exclude` only governs which fields are *re-validated*, never which constraints are skipped. `full_clean()` runs `validate_constraints()`, which **validates `Meta.constraints` `UniqueConstraint`s** (Django 4.1+; the package floor is `Django>=5.2`), so a duplicate is caught **here as a `ValidationError`** with clean field mapping, *before* `save()` (Major-2). Any `ValidationError` populates the `FieldError` envelope and short-circuits to a null-object payload.
5. **Write**: `save()` (create / update) or `delete()`, then assign relations. **Many-to-many write semantics (AR-M1):** an omitted M2M field is left unchanged on update; a *provided* list **replaces** the entire relation set (`instance.<m2m>.set([...])`); a provided empty list clears it; related objects are resolved through the **related model's primary [`DjangoType`][glossary-djangotype] visibility `get_queryset`**, confirming the whole provided set in one `pk__in` query (the target model's default manager only when the related model has no registered primary type), so a hidden member and a missing member are the same indistinguishable field-keyed `FieldError` and a permitted writer can never attach a row they could not see. There is no per-mutation queryset hook in `0.0.11`. A `UniqueConstraint` race that slips past step 4's `validate_constraints()` surfaces here as an `IntegrityError`; the pipeline keys it to the `"__all__"` sentinel rather than raising a 500, as a **documented best-effort race fallback**: `save()`'s `IntegrityError` carries no reliable cross-backend field mapping. It is not the normal unique path and is covered by a mocked-`save()` test so the `fail_under = 100` gate is met without forcing a real concurrent race (Major-2).
6. **Re-fetch / snapshot**: for create / update, re-read the written row **by pk** as a queryset the optimizer plans for the response selection ([Decision 9](#decision-9--optimizer-composition-and-the-spec-035-g2-live-test-handoff)); for delete, that optimizer-planned load **fully materializes the response-selection snapshot — including nested selected relations and connection children (AR-M5)** — *before* step 5's `delete()`, then returns that now-detached in-memory instance (the optimizer plans querysets, not the located instance — see [Edge cases](#edge-cases-and-constraints), Medium-2). The create / update re-fetch is **by pk, without the visibility `get_queryset` filter** — the actor just wrote the row, so round-tripping their own write is not an existence leak ([Decision 9](#decision-9--optimizer-composition-and-the-spec-035-g2-live-test-handoff) owns the GOAL crit-4 tension).
7. **Return** the `<Name>Payload`.

**Relation decode is deferred past Authorize for `create` / `update` (CR-4).** The numbered steps name the *logical* contract order; the implementation runs **Authorize before the relation `GlobalID` decode** (`create`: authorize → decode; `update`: locate → authorize → decode). This is deliberate and strictly better: an unauthorized caller triggers **no** relation `get_queryset` visibility queries and receives **no** field-level decode feedback, so it neither does relation work nor leaks relation visibility before the authorization gate clears. The two pins Decision 15 makes are still honored verbatim — authorize runs **before validation** for `create` (`instance=None`) and **after the step-2 visibility lookup** for `update` / `delete` with the located instance.
